title: Maritime NDT & Class Audit Support | Newport News, VA
description: NDT audit prep for Newport News shipbuilding suppliers: Navy flow-down, Examiner, procedure qualification and class gauging by an ASNT Level III. Ask us.
h1: Maritime NDT Consulting & Class Audit Support in Newport News
html:
This page is written for the fabricators, machine shops, piping suppliers and NDT subcontractors in and around Newport News whose work ends up in Navy ships, and for gauging firms that serve commercial vessels in Hampton Roads. Whether the audit comes from a prime contractor's supplier quality team, the Navy's government inspector or a class society, Atlantis NDT prepares your NDT program for it as an outside ASNT NDT Level III. Send us the purchase order clauses or the audit notice and we will explain what has to change.

A shipyard that sets the terms for a whole region

HII's Newport News Shipbuilding describes itself as the nation's sole designer, builder and refueler of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers. Its fact file credits it with all ten Nimitz-class carriers and more than thirty carriers over seventy-five years, with being the only yard to perform refueling and complex overhaul on Nimitz-class ships, and with handling the inactivation of nuclear carriers, starting with Enterprise. It is also one of only two shipyards able to design and build nuclear-powered submarines, building Virginia-class boats in partnership with General Dynamics Electric Boat and serving as a major shipbuilding partner on the Columbia-class program.

The same fact file calls the yard the largest industrial employer in Virginia, with about 25,000 employees, and notes more than 800 ships delivered to Navy and commercial customers across its history. For an NDT business, scale is the important part. A yard of that size buys enormous quantities of fabricated steel, pipe spools, foundations, castings, machined parts and inspection services, and every purchase order carries quality requirements down the chain. In Newport News, the customer who audits your NDT program is very often that prime contractor, acting on requirements the Navy set.

How Navy NDT requirements reach a Hampton Roads supplier

Most suppliers never read a Navy contract. They read a purchase order, a drawing and a list of referenced specifications, and the NDT obligations hide in those references. When an order calls for NDT under NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, the supplier's own program has to meet that publication: how inspectors are trained, examined and certified, how procedures are written and proven, how equipment is controlled. The drawing or order supplies acceptance criteria. The publication supplies the rules for the people and procedures that apply them.

This chain is where small shops get caught out. A shop that has passed ISO 9001 surveys and customer audits for years can still fail a Navy-flowed NDT review, because the publication asks for things commercial programs rarely contain: recertification by examination rather than by continued service, documented yearly surveillance of each inspector, a tighter near-vision standard, and procedures proven within the shop that uses them. None of it is hard once you know it is there. It becomes hard when you learn about it from a finding. The detail is on our NAVSEA shipyard requirements page.

Two auditors with different questions

Suppliers in Newport News usually meet two kinds of NDT reviewer, and it helps to know which one is in the room.

ReviewerWhy they audit youWhat they focus onWhat a weak answer looks like
Prime contractor supplier qualityYour product is going into their ship, and they answer to the Navy for itWhether your NDT program meets every requirement in their purchase order, and whether your records will survive their own government reviewCertifications issued under a generic written practice that never mentions the Navy publication the order invokes
Government inspector for Navy workAt a private shipyard, the Supervisor of Shipbuilding oversees Navy work, including supplier NDTThe written practice, procedures, personnel records and equipment control behind specific inspectionsA technician who inspected product while their vision test or certification had lapsed
Class society surveyor or approval auditorCommercial ship work and class-credited thickness measurementClass rules, the society's supplier approval scheme and UR Z17Gauging reports from a firm with no approval from that ship's society

The prime's audit usually comes first and is often the harder of the two, because the prime samples aggressively before it lets a new supplier ship anything. Preparing for the prime's audit to the government's standard means you only build the program once.

The Examiner role, and where an outside Level III fits

Under the Navy publication, the person at the center of your NDT program is the Level III Examiner. The Examiner certifies operators and inspectors, writes and signs NDT procedures, and qualifies each procedure by demonstration. Many small suppliers do not employ a Level III and look for an outside one. The publication allows the Examiner's basic and method examinations to come from the employing activity, ASNT or another outside agency, but the specific examination, which covers your products, specifications and written practice, has to be prepared, approved and administered by your activity independently of the Examiner being tested. Whether a particular outside Examiner is acceptable is decided under the publication and by the government inspector, not by the consultant.

Some activities also look at whether a candidate holds an ASNT NDT Level III certificate when they appoint an Examiner. Whether you need it is set by your contract and your customer, so we check that before proposing anyone for the role. What we can always do is write the written practice to the publication, prepare examinations, rebuild personnel files and coach your own staff toward the Examiner role. Our T9074 compliance page lays out the sequence, and written practice development covers the drafting.

Proving a procedure: planning the qualification

A procedure on Navy work is not finished when it is signed. It is qualified by showing that it reliably finds known discontinuities close to the acceptance limit, in material and geometry that represent the product. For suppliers this is often the slowest step, because suitable specimens have to be found or made, documented and kept.

  • Specimen selection: we help you choose specimens that match the product form, thickness range and weld or casting type the procedure covers, with discontinuities of known type, size and location.
  • Documentation: each specimen needs a record of how its discontinuities were made or confirmed, so the qualification can be repeated and defended.
  • The demonstration: the procedure is run as written, by a certified inspector, and the results are compared with the known discontinuities.
  • The record: the qualification report ties procedure revision, specimen, instrument, inspector and results together and is signed by the Examiner.
  • Revision control: if an essential variable changes later, the procedure may need requalification, and the record should show that someone checked.

Our procedure qualification and demonstration service plans and witnesses this work, and procedure development covers writing the procedure in the first place.

Where Atlantis stops: nuclear, radiography and welding

Carriers and submarines built in Newport News are nuclear-powered, and a large share of the yard's work touches the propulsion plant. That work, and the quality assurance regime that governs it, are outside Atlantis's scope. We support suppliers on non-nuclear structure, hull, piping, foundations and outfitting, and we say so at the start of every engagement so nothing is assumed.

Atlantis does not carry out radiographic testing in the US. Suppliers who need RT hire a licensed radiography company, and our Level III can review that company's RT procedure, its images and its personnel records as part of your subcontractor control. We also stay away from welding procedure and welder qualification, which belong to your welding engineer; for background, our WPS, PQR and WPQ guide explains how that side works.

Records that fail supplier audits in Hampton Roads

The NDT findings we help Newport News suppliers close tend to fall into a few groups. None of them are exotic, and all of them are cheaper to fix before the auditor arrives.

  • Certification by service: inspectors whose renewal was signed because they kept working, with no examination behind it.
  • Missing surveillance: no dated record that each inspector's work was witnessed or rechecked during the year.
  • Vision forms: annual tests recorded against a near-vision line the Navy publication does not accept.
  • Imported certifications: a new hire's certificate from a previous employer accepted without recertification by your own activity.
  • Unproven procedures: procedures copied from another company or bought ready-made, used without qualification in your shop.
  • Weak traceability: reports that cannot be tied to a serial-numbered instrument, a procedure revision and a certified person.
  • Subcontractor files: no evidence that you checked the NDT firm you hired before it worked on your product.

Our services for experience logs, training records and certificates and subcontractor approval audits address those groups directly. Shops that lose track of expiry dates can use our certificate tracking app to stop the most common finding of all.

Commercial vessels and class gauging around Newport News

Hampton Roads is also a busy commercial harbor, and bulk carriers, container ships and tankers calling there need thickness measurements when their class surveys come due. If a class surveyor will rely on the readings, IACS UR Z17 requires the gauging firm to be approved by that vessel's society, with thickness measurement approvals renewed at no more than three-year intervals. The society reviews documents, audits the office and witnesses a practical demonstration before issuing a certificate that names the service. Our IACS service supplier approval guide sets out the requirement in full, and UTM operator qualification covers the personnel files a society expects to see.

A Newport News firm working both sides of the river needs to decide whether to run one program to the stricter Navy rules or keep its Navy and commercial programs separate. One program is easier to keep current. Two programs are sometimes cleaner when different people do the two kinds of work. We help you choose and then document the choice so that each auditor sees only what applies to them.

A note on our own position: for its thickness measurement services, our firm is in the process of obtaining class approval under UR Z17 from Lloyd's Register, DNV and ABS. No society has approved us yet, so we prepare firms for class audits but do not offer class-credited gauging ourselves.

How we work with Newport News suppliers

Atlantis keeps no Virginia office. Our Level III consulting is led by our founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in five methods (UT, RT, MT, PT and VT), who has over 11 years of international field experience. Document work is done remotely from Houston, and we come to your shop for qualification demonstrations, mock audits and floor reviews. A typical engagement:

  1. Read the paperwork: purchase orders, drawings, referenced specifications and any supplier quality manual from the prime, so we know exactly which NDT rules apply.
  2. Measure the gap: compare your written practice, procedures, examinations, personnel files and equipment records against those rules, and rank the gaps by audit risk.
  3. Close it: redraft documents for approval by your management and Examiner, build or rebuild examinations, and help collect missing evidence.
  4. Prove it: plan and witness procedure qualifications and run a mock supplier audit in your shop.
  5. Answer findings: after the prime's or the government's review, help write corrective actions with cause, correction and objective evidence.

Your company certifies its people and owns its records, the prime decides whether to approve you as a supplier, and the government inspector decides whether your program meets the publication. We prepare you for those decisions; we do not make them.

What to send us

  • The purchase order quality clauses and the specifications they reference, or the prime's audit notice and checklist.
  • Your written practice, plus a list of the methods and levels it covers.
  • Your NDT procedures, with any qualification records.
  • Three personnel files with examinations, vision tests and surveillance records.
  • Equipment and calibration records, and two recent inspection reports.
  • Any earlier audit findings and the responses you gave.

We reply within one business day. If the gap is in technician skills rather than paperwork, see maritime NDT training in Newport News or the Newport News NDT training page.

Newport News supplier readiness checklist

  1. Find every NDT-related specification your purchase orders reference and confirm which ones govern people and procedures.
  2. Confirm that your written practice names the Navy publication where your orders invoke it.
  3. Identify your Examiner and confirm how their specific examination was prepared and administered.
  4. Check that every procedure used on Navy-flowed work has a qualification record from your shop.
  5. Bring each inspector's recertification, surveillance and vision records up to date.
  6. Recertify any new hire who joined with a certificate from another employer.
  7. Review your radiography subcontractor and any other NDT subcontractor files.
  8. If you gauge commercial ships, confirm your class approvals and their expiry dates.

For the national overview, see maritime NDT audit support. Across the water, our Portsmouth, Virginia page covers contractors at the public naval shipyard, and the Groton page covers the submarine supply chain in New England. Broader Level III work in the city is on our Newport News consulting page.

faq.q: Our purchase order from a shipbuilder references a NAVSEA NDT publication. What does that change for us?
faq.a: Your NDT program has to meet that publication for the work on that order: written practice, inspector training, examination and certification, procedure qualification and equipment control. The drawing or order still gives the acceptance criteria. See T9074 audit preparation.

faq.q: Who audits a supplier's NDT for Navy work at a private shipyard?
faq.a: Usually the prime contractor's supplier quality team first. The Navy's Supervisor of Shipbuilding oversees Navy work at private yards and can also review supplier NDT. A class society is involved only for class work, not for Navy work.

faq.q: Can an outside Level III be our Examiner?
faq.a: The publication allows outside agencies to examine an Examiner on the basic and method parts, but your activity must prepare, approve and administer the specific examination independently of that person. Acceptance of a particular outside Examiner is decided under the publication and by the government inspector. We check this before proposing anyone.

faq.q: Do we need the ASNT Naval Shipbuilders Level III certification?
faq.a: Only if your contract or customer requires it. Some activities look for it when appointing an Examiner. We confirm the requirement from your order and customer before planning around it.

faq.q: Does Atlantis support suppliers on nuclear propulsion components?
faq.a: No. Naval nuclear propulsion work and its quality assurance regime are outside our scope. We support non-nuclear structure, hull, piping, foundations and outfitting.

faq.q: Can a procedure we already use for commercial work be used on Navy-flowed orders?
faq.a: Possibly, but only after your Examiner approves it for that work and it has been qualified in your shop by demonstrating detection of known discontinuities near the acceptance limit. Procedures do not transfer between activities without NAVSEA approval.

faq.q: Will Atlantis do the radiography on our parts?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not carry out radiographic testing in the US. Hire a licensed radiography company, then let our Level III check its procedure, images and personnel records for your subcontractor file.

faq.q: Does Atlantis come to our shop in Newport News?
faq.a: Yes, for procedure qualifications, mock audits and floor reviews. The document side is handled remotely from Houston, and we travel to Hampton Roads for the rest.

faq.q: Is Atlantis class-approved for thickness measurement?
faq.a: Not yet. We are in the process of obtaining that approval from all three of Lloyd's Register, DNV and ABS, and hold no class certificate at present.

faq.q: What is the quickest way to reduce audit risk before a supplier review?
faq.a: Check dates and signatures first: certifications, vision tests, surveillance records and equipment calibration. Then confirm that every procedure in use has a qualification record. Those two steps remove most of the findings we see. Our audit documentation service can do the check with you.
